audit.conclusion: The current assignment explicitly requires machine-wide aggregation; existing per-package reservation tests express the superseded behavior and were updated before RED. Item 2.33 remained unchanged after concurrent root merge. Other open tasks remain; no archive or checkbox changes.

behavior.delivery: Each completion retains a separate durable package. One oldest open event represents all unbound packages, with deduplicated runIds; pending sibling intents are removed transactionally before delivery. Delivered/uncertain receipts retain existing retry behavior. Already acknowledged events are not recreated.
behavior.reservation: One or several assigned context-review.due references select one reservation; its input includes every open package. All package rows bind under a savepoint to the same reviewer. Existing UNIQUE index migrates to a nonunique lookup index. production-runtime.ts:1534-1537 writes review.runIds and corresponding traces into context-review-input.json.
behavior.duringReview: Any open bound package suppresses due events and parallel reservation. Later packages remain unbound; after success the bound snapshot closes, and the next delivery stages one event for the waiting packages. Failure releases the entire bound snapshot for retry.

findings: The pending-event helper has one responsibility: read open packages, reject an active review, return the deduplicated runId union. Inputs and output explicitly identify the database and event.
Reservation guards missing references and an active reviewer, binds the snapshot in a savepoint, and returns the exact runIds used by production input export; failure rolls back bindings.

Delivery explicitly normalizes the pending queue in its existing transaction before receipt handling. Current payload is updated without creating duplicate health events. Missing acknowledged events remain absent.
Lifecycle completion derives the aggregate pending event after reviewer settlement; no new configuration, limits, timeout or user-visible labels were added.

Behavior preservation is evidenced by the final 36-test group, including failed reports, cleanup, journal failure, receipt recovery, migrated unique index, multi-reference assignment and waiting packages. git diff --check passed.
